rites.name: Osulareno
rites.text: Osulareno is the concept of a low, humming resonance that moved through Kelaneld during the Singing, when the first roots of the world began to condense out of sound. It is less a force than a pattern, a rhythm the early ground learned to repeat until it held together. Its role in the Record is to mark the moment when the world first became something that could be stood upon.

rites.name: Gougurn
rites.text: Gougurn is a concept within Kelaneld, a sounding-pattern that the first roots of the world seem to hum as they condense in the Singing. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall split old bonds apart, Gougurn was the rhythm that held loose stone together long enough to settle. It is less a force than a memory of how ground chooses to stay put.

rites.name: Kaluvanala
rites.text: Kaluvanala is the concept of the sovereign's sworn bond, a binding of grove and kingdom that held through the Sundering of worlds and the breaking of the Shards. In the Age of the first sovereign it was the promise that roots would outlast the fracture of the land.

rites.name: Tauneornum
rites.text: Tauneornum is the Walled Age concept of holding a line, the discipline by which Kelaneld's builders kept walls standing for centuries through orders, church rites and the first careful crossings of rivers. It is less a force than a habit of patience that the realm's people carried into every task. Its sign is the mortared stone that refuses to shift under the weight it was set to bear.

rites.name: Kharnoth
rites.text: Kharnoth is a concept in the Kelaneld Walled Age, an idea of a wall that is held rather than built, passed between orders of keepers. It came to mark the years of the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between the walled holds and their keepers.

rites.name: Joradoldath
rites.text: Joradoldath is a martial discipline in Kelaneld, taught in the grounded era's guild halls to those whose arms carry enough strength to bear a blade's full weight. Practitioners who sharpen their stance with a familiar weapon find their strikes gain precision and bite, letting a steady hand turn ordinary steel into a decisive instrument.

rites.name: Crudosteld
rites.text: Crudosteld is a stubborn, rust-colored mineral-tinted ironwood that grows along the cliffs of Kelaneld's low valleys. Its sap hardens into a brittle sheen that artisans use to lend wielded blades a single heavier, more decisive blow. Its energies stay within the grounded scale of hand tools and small war-engines.

rites.name: Elamiona
rites.text: Elamiona is a concept of Kelaneld, set in the Holy Age, when temples and orders kept watch over flame and the Library shelved every possible ending. It exists as an idea that the orders invoke to justify their rites and their rivalries. Its power is measured in the small, controlled fires and wards its adherents can raise.

rites.name: Vhoggazhok
rites.text: Vhoggazhok is a concept in the Kelaneld universe, a branching idea of the Three Futures where the Library files every possible ending. It came to prominence during the Age of Sundering, when landfall split old allegiances apart and people argued over which outcome to keep.
